subject: Segmented VPC rollout and staged on-prem capacity onboarding (renewal coordination)
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@medicore.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, John Liu <john.liu@medicore.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets

Hi Markus / John,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we discussed, Medicore is planning to renew in June and we'd like to add a second isolated VPC for analytics plus two on-prem clusters for edge inference at our regional lab sites. Attached is a high-level forecast (provisioning matrix) with expected peak tokens and desired concurrency per environment.

Key asks from our side:
- Proposed sequencing so we can keep existing production stable.
- Isolation approach for the analytics VPC (network/tenant-level).
- Estimated lead times for provisioning dedicated nodes in our on-prem sites.

I'll loop procurement after we agree on sequencing. Attachment: medicore_provisioning_matrix_v2.xlsx

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Head of Platform, Medicore Health
[sarah.park@medicore.com]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@medicore.com>, John Liu <john.liu@medicore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets

Thanks Sarah — got the matrix and good detail. High level response and suggestions below; I'll set up a short sync once we align on sequencing.

Proposal (draft):
1) Phase A (0-30 days post-renewal): analytics VPC (isolated tenant). Keep model variants identical to prod, enable KV-prefix caching to speed warmup.
2) Phase B (30-60 days): provision first on-prem cluster at Lab-East (smaller footprint, can act as a canary).
3) Phase C (60-120 days): provision second on-prem cluster at Lab-West + finalize network ACLs and audit logging.

Open questions for Medicore:
- Can you confirm target concurrency for each on-prem cluster in the attached matrix? (I see ranges; we need final numbers to size GPU pools.)
- Any regulatory constraints requiring air-gapped transport between clusters?

Next steps: Monica will draft a provisioning runbook and Priyom will scope the maintenance windows. If procurement needs draft amendment language, we can provide a clause for phased delivery and acceptance criteria.

-Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, John Liu <john.liu@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets

Markus / John — quick technical notes to shape Phase A/B: 

Phase A (analytics VPC):
- We recommend separate tenant IDs and strict policy routing (no cross-tenant KV cache).
- Enable prefix-caching for the first 8 tokens to reduce repeat cost on analytics workloads.
- Retain 30 days of telemetry for the new VPC; we can increase retention as needed (billing implication).

Phase B (Lab-East on-prem):
- Start with 2x T4-equivalent nodes (quantized weights) to validate latency targets.
- Network: small jumpbox + mTLS between Redwood agent and customer gateway.
- Acceptance: throughput validation (75th percentile) and automated failover to hosted model if local nodes degrade.

Notes: If Medicore requires physical airgap for Lab-West, that will change provisioning lead times and we'll need signed acceptance on connectivity constraints. Priyom — can you outline ops windows and bootstrap timeline?

- Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@medicore.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: John Liu <john.liu@medicore.com>, Procurement <procure@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets

Thanks — this looks reasonable. A few clarifications: 
- Concurrency: Lab-East target 120 concurrent requests; Lab-West 240. Analytics VPC peak concurrency 600 but low sustained.
- Airgap: Lab-West must be effectively air-gapped for PHI-processing windows; we can allow batched syncs overnight via removable media but no persistent network egress during business hours.
- Procurement timeline: we need final amendment signed by 2027-06-10 to meet internal budget cutoffs.

I'll attach a placeholder PO once procurement confirms. For the airgap constraint, please flag any limitations on the Redwood agent.

Attachment: PO_placeholder_v1.pdf (will send real PO next week)

— Sarah

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@medicore.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets

Quick ops reply on windows and lead times: 
- Provisioning lead time for on-prem kit (airgap-compatible): 6-8 weeks from signed amendment due to shipping and validation.
- For non-airgapped cluster (Lab-East) we can schedule a 2-week bootstrap once credentials and gateway are ready.
- Maintenance windows: propose Tue/Wed 01:00-04:00 local time for initial bootstrapping to avoid daytime traffic.

Staggering suggestion to reduce risk: Spin up Lab-East first (canary), run 2 full-week load tests, then proceed with Lab-West but with airgap procedures (overnight sync testing).

I'll prepare a calendar proposal for the windows and a minimal runbook for the airgapped acceptances.

- Priyom

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@medicore.com>, John Liu <john.liu@medicore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window: VPC segmentation + on-prem capacity targets — next steps

Sarah / John — thanks for the clarity. Summarizing agreed timeline and immediate asks so procurement has what it needs: 

Agreed timeline (conditional on signed amendment):
- Week 0 (post-sign): finalize concurrency numbers and provide gateway creds.
- Weeks 1-2: provision analytics VPC, enable telemetry + prefix caching.
- Weeks 3-4: provision Lab-East on-prem cluster (non-airgapped) + run canary load testing.
- Weeks 6-10: ship airgap-compatible kit for Lab-West, onsite validation + acceptance.

Documentation to attach to amendment: provisioning matrix (received), staged acceptance criteria (we will draft), and maintenance window calendar. Monica and Priyom will attach the runbook and acceptance checklist by EOD Monday.

Related items: INF-3421 is the Jira ticket we will use for rollout tracking and the Drive folder will contain runbooks and the amendment draft. Procurement — if you need a contract clause sample for phased delivery and acceptance, we have language we can drop into the SOW.

Next step: Markus to coordinate a 30-minute sync Wednesday to move procurement and schedule bootstraps.

Attachments to follow: signed-amendment-draft.docx (draft for review)

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
